findings.description: A one-alarm fire struck this four-storey, 126-unit apartment building near 15th Street, across from the Armory, at 10:30 p.m. on Saturday 29 August 2026. It started in a single fourth-floor unit and was put out without incident, but the evacuation took time because many of the building's residents are elderly. Five people were taken to hospital and twelve were displaced; nine households were put up in hotels for a week by the Human Services Agency while fire and water damage was dealt with. The fire department attributed the likely cause to a scooter. No resident is named or described here.

citation.label: Mission Local, “5 hospitalized, a dozen displaced in Mission District apartment fire,” 31 August 2026

findings.description: Sin Miedo, an art gallery run by the nonprofit Sketchboard Co. with programming from the printing company Golden Gate Co-op, takes the storefront here near 24th Street, next door to the bookstore and gallery Et al. The space had housed Climate Control Gallery until it closed earlier in the month. The gallery is to open on Saturday 19 September 2026 and run Thursdays to Mondays, with classes, workshops, a library and a shop. Dated to the article rather than to the opening, which had not happened when it was written.

findings.description: The Portal Cinema, a nonprofit single-screen repertory theatre with 45 seats, is to open here near 29th Street in October 2026. It is to run more than eleven showings a week — repertory, new releases, contemporary work from abroad and artists' moving image — and to be equipped for DCP, 35mm and 16mm projection. Dated to the article; the cinema's own site gives only the month.

findings.description: Four murals on this building's Clarion Alley wall were painted over on a Monday in late August 2026, three of them completely and one in part, after the property's owner ordered an employee to paint out what had been reported as graffiti. The Clarion Alley Mural Project, which has managed murals in the alley for thirty-four years and holds verbal agreements with the alley's owners, says it is unclear whether it had a written agreement for this building; the murals can be restored at a cost it has not yet established. The four were a 2016 memorial, a 2015 tribute to Adobe Books' former home, a tribute to a graffiti artist, and a mural painted this spring by students from Graffiti Camp for Girls. The article gives the day only as "last Monday", so the entry takes the publication date; the owner is a private trust and is not recorded here.

citation.label: Mission Local, “‘My boss told me to’ said man painting over murals in Clarion Alley,” 1 September 2026
